topics.topic: Authority, instant, representation, and read count for marked_at
questions: What authority supplies `marked_at`, what instant does it denote, what datetime representation is stored, and how many times may one mark operation read that authority?
What clock supplies marked_at, what datetime representation is stored, and how many readings does one mark operation take?

judgement.why: This is the same question about marked_at authority, instant, representation and read count already decided by P7, and the relevant passages are unchanged.

precedent.topic: Source, representation, timezone convention, and read count for marked_at
quotes:
1. The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

2. Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

3. The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form. It sets `marked_at`.
precedent.why: The unchanged A7 passages already decide the clock authority, representation, reading count and replay behavior, and the reopening change did not touch or affect them.

topics.topic: Camera timestamp field precedence, validity, fallback, and UTC conversion for taken_at
questions: Which camera metadata field is authoritative, how are multiple camera date fields ordered, and when is a camera value considered unavailable or invalid so that file modification time is used?
Which exact camera metadata field or ordered set of fields supplies taken_at, and how is a camera value without an offset converted to UTC?

quotes:
3. The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.

4. The photo date is delivered as UTC without an offset, as the Client Portal stores it. A camera
   time with no offset is read in the configured time zone. A local time that occurs twice is the
   first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
   the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
judgement.why: A2 specifies the ordered camera fields, offset source, invalidity and plausibility rules, fallback, local-time edge cases and UTC conversion.

topics.topic: Definition and handling of damaged or schema-invalid placement records under A6 rule 5
questions: Does A6 rule 5 also refuse a record that has every field but contains a wrong field type, an invalid enumeration value, a malformed UUID or hash, or unexpected extra fields?
When a valid placement exists but its mark record is damaged, does delivery replay the placement or refuse the whole operation with STATE_UNAVAILABLE?

quotes: M04, or nothing when its record does not exist.
`state_unavailable` for a damaged record.

`capability:delivery_store.read_placement` and `capability:delivery_store.read_mark` read both records, so a
   damaged record stops the delivery. With an existing placement the flow answers `replayed`, with the `photo_id` of
   its mark if there is one.
judgement.why: The later public operation can return only a typed M04 or absence and returns state_unavailable for a damaged record, while the delivery flow expressly reads both records and stops on either damaged record.

topics.topic: Filesystem modification-time observation, read count, and snapshot consistency
questions: When EXIF time is unavailable, from which filesystem observation is the modification time taken, how many times is it read, and must it belong to the same opened file whose bytes are prepared?
How many times may the operation read the camera timestamp or file modification time, and must that metadata belong to the same opened-file snapshot as the bytes?

quotes:
3. The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.

3. One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, a relative path in the form a scan reports, and
   `source_id`. The service keeps no memory of earlier scans: it judges the name and the file when the call
   runs. The named file is read once, and the bytes that were read are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.

Syncthing may change the folder during a scan, so a scan is not a view of one instant. Each rule applies
to what its step finds when it runs, and the next scan sees the folder as it then stands.

4. A file's modification time is converted to the same form before it is compared or delivered, dropping
   any fraction finer than a microsecond toward the earlier instant.
judgement.divergence: One implementation uses modification-time metadata read from the path before replacement, while another uses metadata belonging to the opened file whose bytes are prepared; the Portal user sees a different photo date for the same stored pixels.
judgement.why: The texts specify the time's precedence and representation and a single byte read, but do not bind the modification-time observation to that opened file or limit its own read count.

topics.topic: Required pre-state, outcome, and persistence assertions for the INV-06 recovery test
questions: What exact pre-state proves that no A6 rule 5 refusal applies, which delivery status must the retry return, and which stored-image and placement-record assertions must the test make to show INV-06?
What must this test assert: the returned status, whether the stored image is rewritten, the exact number and validity of records and images, and the state left by the first failed call?

quotes: - INV-06: at most one placement exists per project and source content, and a repeated placement writes nothing.

- INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged, with one placement record in place (`test_a_repeated_placement_writes_no_durable_state`). When no refusal of A6 rule 5 applies, a delivery repeated after a failed record write completes the placement (`test_a_delivery_repeated_after_a_failed_record_write_completes`).

After condition 5 a stored image may remain without a record: no caller has received
   its reference, and a repeated delivery of the same file writes it again and completes the placement,
   unless a refusal of A6 rule 5 applies.

3. Each file is written to a temporary name in its folder, synchronised to disk and renamed, and
   its folder is synchronised, so a reader sees a complete file or none. Atomicity is per file. A3
   decides what a crash between the image and the record means.
judgement.divergence: One test accepts any successful retry described as completing the placement, while another requires an image-only pre-state, a `placed` result, another image write and exactly one valid placement record and stored image; the test suite and storage operator notice implementations that pass one specification but fail the other.
judgement.why: The recovery Required tests item says only that the retry completes the placement and does not state the precise failed-call pre-state, returned status or durable-state assertions needed to demonstrate INV-06.

events: The caller repeats delivery of the same source.
The recovery test observes the returned outcome and durable files.
outcomes: The test accepts the retry merely because a placement can be read afterward.
The test requires `placed`, verifies that the image was written again, and verifies exactly one valid image and one valid placement record.
witness.observer: The test suite and an operator observing durable writes
basis:
After condition 5 a stored image may remain without a record: no caller has received
   its reference, and a repeated delivery of the same file writes it again and completes the placement,
   unless a refusal of A6 rule 5 applies.

- INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged, with one placement record in place (`test_a_repeated_placement_writes_no_durable_state`). When no refusal of A6 rule 5 applies, a delivery repeated after a failed record write completes the placement (`test_a_delivery_repeated_after_a_failed_record_write_completes`).

topics.topic: Retry behavior when record writing reports failure after leaving a valid record
questions: If writing the record reports an error after a complete valid record has already been renamed or synchronised, is the first call failed, and must the repeated call replay that record or create the placement again?

If a record-write call reports failure but nevertheless leaves a complete readable placement record, must the repeated delivery replay without writing under rule 2 or write the image again under rule 5?

quotes:
2. Delivering content that already has a placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the

4. Checks run in this order: token, request form and project id, connection, photo folder, source id,

judgement.why: The write error makes the first call failed, but a complete readable record is an existing placement checked before the source file, so the retry replays without writing; the write-again rule addresses the stated case where only an image remains without a record.

When no refusal of A6 rule 5 applies, a delivery repeated after a failed record write completes the placement (`test_a_delivery_repeated_after_a_failed_record_write_completes`).
